chunks: Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام ruled regarding the teeth for which the diyyah is apportioned that they are twenty-eight teeth: sixteen in the back of the mouth and twelve in its front.
So the compensation for each tooth from the front teeth, when it is broken such that it is lost, is fifty dinars, making that six hundred dinars.
And the compensation for each tooth from the back teeth, when it is broken such that it is lost, is half the compensation of the front teeth: twenty-five dinars, making that four hundred dinars.
Thus that is one thousand dinars. Whatever is less than this has no diyyah, and whatever is more than this has no diyyah.

key_terms.الدِّيَةُ: blood money or legal financial compensation for injury
key_terms.الْأَسْنَانِ: the teeth subject to legal compensation
key_terms.دِينَارًا: a dinar; the monetary unit used to quantify the compensation
key_terms.مَقَادِيمِهِ: the front part of the mouth, meaning the front teeth
key_terms.مَوَاخِيرِ الْفَمِ: the back teeth of the mouth

ai.seo_question: What is the diyyah for front and back teeth according to Imam Ali عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith records a legal ruling from Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib عليه السلام on the fixed diyyah for teeth. It specifies the number of front and back teeth counted in compensation and assigns different monetary values to each category, with the total reaching one thousand dinars.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5300 - Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) ruled regarding the teeth for which blood money (diyyah) is divided that they are twenty-eight in total - sixteen in back of the mouth and twelve in the front.
The compensation for each of the front teeth, if broken and completely lost, is fifty dinars, totaling six hundred dinars.
The compensation for each of the back teeth, if broken and completely lost, is half the amount of the front teeth, which is twenty-five dinars, totaling four hundred dinars.
Altogether, the full compensation for all these teeth is one thousand dinars. Anything less than this has no diyyah, and anything more has no diyyah.
